statement: Night-time-light indicators are experimental statistics: they complement official statistics and do not replace them. Every output is published with its method, validation, uncertainty, limitations and a confidence level.

use_cases.title: Time dynamics
use_cases.question: Is activity accelerating or slowing down, net of seasonality?
use_cases.method: Robust STL (period 12) on log(sum of lights); Theil–Sen slope and Mann–Kendall test on annual composites; anomaly and break detection.
use_cases.limits: Cloud cover and short summer nights; light is not value added.

use_cases.title: Regional growth and convergence
use_cases.question: Which regions take off, which fall behind?
use_cases.method: Robust growth per unit (Theil–Sen, Mann–Kendall), growth/stagnation/decline classes, β- and σ-convergence, Herfindahl index.

validation.text: Rank correlation with tropospheric NO₂ (independent source)

use_cases.uncertainty: Class assigned only if |slope| ≥ threshold and p < α; CI of β (robust errors).
use_cases.limits: Small units: noise and light blooming between neighbours.
use_cases.confidence_reason: classification of 12 units, threshold ±1%/yr and p < 0.10

use_cases.title: Light–GDP relationship
use_cases.question: Can growth be estimated before its release, and regional GDP?
use_cases.method: log(light) ~ log(GDP) in levels and growth, OLS with HAC errors; out-of-sample nowcast; regional GDP = national GDP allocated pro rata of light.
use_cases.uncertainty: 95% CI of the elasticity: 1.24 to 3.18; 80% and 95% prediction intervals.
use_cases.limits: Short annual sample; regional GDP is an experimental statistic to be checked against regional accounts.

use_cases.title: Shocks and resilience
use_cases.question: How deep was a shock, and how fast the recovery?
use_cases.method: Gap to the pre-shock level on the seasonally adjusted series; structural breaks; daily Black Marble index.

validation.text: Does the trough exceed ordinary variability?

use_cases.uncertainty: Pre-shock month-to-month variability (robust SD); unexplained breaks flagged.
use_cases.limits: Shocks hitting poorly lit activities (agriculture, daytime services) are underestimated.
use_cases.confidence_reason: trough compared with pre-shock month-to-month variability

use_cases.title: Inequality and electrification
use_cases.question: Where do people without electricity live?
use_cases.method: Population-weighted Gini and Theil; population of inhabited pixels below the detection threshold; sensitivity to three thresholds; bootstrap CI of the Gini change.

validation.text: Gap with the World Bank electricity-access rate

use_cases.uncertainty: Range across radiance thresholds; bootstrap CI of the Gini.
use_cases.limits: Proxy of outdoor lighting, not of connection: a connected but dimly lit household looks “in the dark”.
use_cases.confidence_reason: sensitive to the radiance threshold (from 0.00 to 0.00 M depending on the threshold); a proxy for outdoor lighting, not for grid connection

use_cases.title: Industrial zones
use_cases.question: Where is industry, and is its activity growing?
use_cases.method: Concordance of six signals per pixel (≥ 3 including light), 8-connected clusters, typology and confidence.
use_cases.uncertainty: Per-cluster confidence from the number of strong signals; isolated sites to verify.
use_cases.limits: Sentinel-5P (≈ 5 km) and MODIS (1 km) resolution: signals describe a neighbourhood.
use_cases.confidence_reason: no reference list available to validate the detection

use_cases.title: Seasonal tourism
use_cases.question: Which areas live from tourism, and how does the season evolve?
use_cases.method: Summer excess net of comparable units at the same latitude; one-sided test; season index base 100; seasons overlapping Ramadan flagged.
use_cases.uncertainty: p-value per unit; 2020–2021 excluded from the classification.
use_cases.limits: Any summer activity (diaspora, second homes, festivals) is captured, not only tourism.
use_cases.confidence_reason: no hotel-night statistics to validate the indicator

use_cases.title: Urbanisation signals
use_cases.question: Where do cities spread, where do villages get electrified, and where does population grow without light?
use_cases.method: Lit area (pixels above the threshold) and population per unit; Theil–Sen growth rates; newly lit pixels (dark two years in a row at the start, lit two years in a row at the end), split between electrification of inhabited areas and new settlements; light/population typology.

validation.text: Rank correlation with GHSL built-up area growth (independent source)

use_cases.uncertainty: Persistence required over two years to limit noise; ± 1 pp margin between growth rates before classifying.
use_cases.limits: Light measures outdoor lighting, not urbanisation in the administrative sense; blooming widens cities; GHSL population is interpolated between epochs.
use_cases.confidence_reason: rank correlation of 0.39 with GHSL built-up growth (11 units)

dqaf.evidence: African Development Bank × Data Innovation for Africa (DI4A) project; free satellite data; explicit policy question for each use case.
Open code, documented methods, parameters and versions recorded in the manifest; no individual data; publication without manual intervention on figures.

dqaf.practice: Concepts, scope, classification, basis for recording
dqaf.evidence: Methods published in the literature (Henderson et al. 2012; Elvidge et al. 2021; Román et al. 2018); ISO 3166 codes; geoBoundaries; WGS 84.

dqaf.practice: Source data, assessment, statistical techniques, validation, revisions
dqaf.evidence: Quality control (cloud cover, gas flares, outliers); validation of every use case against an independent source; confidence intervals; published confidence level.
Monthly series available a few weeks after the month; full recomputation at each run (time-stamped cache); monthly/annual consistency checked.
Public bilingual dashboard, open files (CSV, JSON, GeoJSON), metadata manifest, AI agent citing its sources, GitHub repository with citation.

gsbpm.what: Policy questions of the eight use cases
Choice of sources, indicators and thresholds
ISO3-driven pipeline, embedded code, tests on a synthetic dataset
Earth Engine, World Bank, OpenStreetMap — with caching
Clouds, gas flares, outliers, harmonisation, quality control
Eight use cases, validation, uncertainty, interpretation
Dashboard, images, AI agent, GitHub repository
Quality sheets, confidence levels, limitations, recommendations

fair.how: Public GitHub repository with description, topics and CITATION.cff; metadata manifest; persistent identifier possible (Zenodo DOI).
Public HTTPS without authentication; open formats; code and data under an explicit licence.
CSV, JSON, GeoJSON (WGS 84); ISO 3166 codes; stable unit identifiers; documented indicator vocabulary.
Provenance (sources, versions, parameters), licences, methods and limitations published with the results.

un_principles.how: Indicators useful to decision-makers, released to everyone at the same time.
Published scientific methods, choices based on technical criteria.
Confidence levels, limitations and an “experimental” label on every output.
No individual data: territorial aggregates only.
Open code, reusable by every statistical office.

experimental: All series and maps derived from night-time lights
Estimated regional GDP and growth estimate for the unpublished year
Population “in the dark” (proxy of electricity access)
Industrial clusters and tourist season index
